sentences.text: Piveteausaurus is a theropod dinosaur known from a partial skull found in the Middle Jurassic Marnes de Dives of northern France. The braincase of this animal is comparable in size to that of a large Allosaurus.
In 2012, Thomas Holtz estimated that Piveteausaurus could have reached a length of 11 meters.

The partial braincase that serves as the type specimen for Piveteausaurus was first described in 1923 by the French paleontologist Jean Piveteau. The type specimen was found by local collector Dutacq in the Marnes de Dives near Dives in Normandy, France.
The rocks containing the fossils were later reevaluated as being from the Upper Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 164 million years ago.
The genus was established in 1977 by Philippe Taquet and Samuel Welles and named in honor of Jean Piveteau.
Piveteausaurus is classified within the family Megalosauridae and belongs to the subfamily Eustreptospondylinae.
A 2010 analysis by Benson found that Piveteausaurus most likely belonged to the family Megalosauridae, though its exact placement remained unresolved.
Piveteausaurus lived during the Callovian to Oxfordian stages, between 165.3 and 154.8 million years ago.
